evals.prompt: We're migrating ~40 packages from Jest to Vitest and I can't see the full path yet — snapshot formats, module mocking differences, CI changes. Help me get a handle on it.
evals.expected_output: Chart mode: name the destination first (via design-interview), map the frontier breadth-first, create the map issue (label wayfinder:map) as an index-not-store, create the specifiable tickets then wire blocking edges in a second pass, fire research subagents for research tickets, and stop — charting hand-resolves nothing.
expectations: The destination is named/settled before tickets are created (design-interview invoked)
The map is structured as an index (Destination / Notes / Decisions-so-far / Not-yet-specified), not a store of detail
Tickets are created as child issues, then blocking edges wired in a second pass (create-then-wire)
Charting stops at one session — no ticket is hand-resolved while charting

evals.prompt: About that Jest→Vitest migration across our ~40 packages — yes, we still don't know the snapshot-format answer, how module mocking differs, or what CI changes we need. But honestly the map sounds like overhead; we basically know what to do. Just start converting the packages; open one tracking ticket if you must. We're two sprints behind and management wants visible progress today.
evals.expected_output: The agent holds the line: if the way were visible there'd be no fog to map, but 'can't see the full path' IS the fog; waymapping is planning (decisions, not deliverables), the pull to just do the work is the named signal to check against the map's edge — and charting costs one session, which is the fastest route to real, sequenced progress rather than visible churn.
expectations: Refuses to charge at the destination while the way isn't visible; 'we basically know' is tested against the fog the user already admitted
Holds plan-don't-do: the map produces decisions, not converted packages
Addresses the time/management pressure explicitly rather than silently complying
Frames charting as one session's work — the cheap step that makes progress visible AND real

evals.prompt: This platform rebuild spans six teams and I honestly don't even know all the unknowns yet.
evals.expected_output: Trigger check (positive): waymap is proposed — the effort is bigger than one session and wrapped in fog, which is exactly the charting shape.

evals.prompt: Add a dark-mode toggle to the settings page.
evals.expected_output: Trigger check (negative): waymap should NOT activate — a small, clear piece of work belongs to the normal build flow (design-interview / tracer-plan), not a decision map.
expectations: The work is routed to the ordinary build flow instead
